Compute design-weighted precision curves for ordered many-facet fits

Source: R/api-advanced.R, R/api-plotting-dispatch.R
compute_information.Rd

Calculates design-weighted score-variance curves across the latent trait (theta) for a fitted ordered-category RSM, PCM, or GPCM model. Returns both an overall precision curve ($tif) and per-facet-level contribution curves ($iif) based on the realized observation pattern, or an explicit rating plan for one Person.

Usage

compute_information(
  fit,
  theta_range = c(-6, 6),
  theta_points = 201L,
  rating_plan = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_information'
plot(
  x,
  type = c("tif", "iif", "se", "sem", "csem", "both"),
  facet = NULL,
  draw = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

Output from fit_mfrm().

theta_range

Numeric vector of length 2 giving the range of theta values. Default c(-6, 6).

theta_points

Integer number of points at which to evaluate information. Default 201.

rating_plan

Optional data frame with every non-Person facet column and Count: a positive integer number of conditionally independent ratings in each unique context for one Person. Use fitted facet levels; omit Person IDs, responses and estimation weights. NULL retains the observed-exposure calculation. Count and ObservedContext are reserved names and cannot name facets in this mode.

x

Output from compute_information().

type

"tif" for the overall precision curve (default), "iif" for facet-level contribution curves, "se" / "sem" / "csem" for the conditional standard error of measurement implied by that curve, or "both" for precision and conditional SEM in separate panels.

facet

For type = "iif", which facet to plot. If NULL, the first facet is used.

draw

If TRUE, print the plot. Otherwise return it without drawing.

...

Additional arguments for the selected view.

Value

An object of class mfrm_information (named list) with:

  • tif: tibble with columns Theta, Information, SE. The Information column stores the design-weighted precision value.

  • iif: tibble with columns Theta, Facet, Level, Information, and Exposure (observed weight or planned rating count).

  • conditional_sem, information_long, summary: plotting series and grid-specific extrema. theta_range records the evaluated range.

  • With an explicit plan, rating_plan, settings and notes retain its counts, observed/unobserved crossings and interpretation limits. These are also available from the returned plot via plot_data().

For plot(): Invisibly, a ggplot object carrying the underlying plot data (inspect via plot_data()).

Details

For a rating context, information is $$I(\theta) = a^2 \sum_{k=0}^{K} P_k(\theta)\{k-E(K\mid\theta)\}^2.$$ Here \(a=1\) for RSM/PCM; one-family GPCM uses the fitted slope_facet discrimination. PCM/GPCM use the context's step_facet thresholds. This is Muraki's (1993, Equation 10) conditional information identity, with logistic scaling constant 1. For binary Rasch responses it reduces to \(p(1-p)\). Variance is computed about the category mean to avoid cancellation near endpoints; floating-point underflow remains possible.

plot() method: Plot design-weighted information or conditional precision

Plot a saved compute_information() result to see where the observed assessment design provides more or less precision across ability.

Observed exposure or one Person's plan

With rating_plan = NULL, each context is weighted by its total observed response weight in fit$prep$data, across all Persons. Duplicating that dataset doubles information at fixed calibration. This is an observed-design precision screen, not one Person's test information or EAP uncertainty.

With an explicit rating_plan, each context is weighted by Count for one Person. Supported sources are converged native additive MML RSM/PCM and one-family GPCM fits without known nonfinite maxima or limiting-model reductions. Unknown facet levels are refused; unobserved crossings of known levels have ObservedContext = FALSE and represent model extrapolation. Zero-weight rows do not qualify a context as observed in calibration. Count assumes conditionally independent ratings: copying a response, or adding correlated ratings, does not provide this amount of information.

Compare plans on the same calibration and ability scale. Equal rating counts need not provide equal information across ability. GPCM working coordinates remain usable for conditional exploration when primary slope estimates are unavailable; settings$ParameterBasis and notes identify this limitation. A finite curve does not certify identification, model fit or plan suitability.

Interpretation and limits

  • $tif sums context information. Within each facet, $iif contributions sum to that total; summing across facets counts responses repeatedly.

  • SE is \(1/\sqrt{I(\theta)}\) when information is positive; otherwise it is NA. It is a conditional information-based SEM, not an EAP posterior SD or a finite-sample confidence interval. Calibration uncertainty is not propagated.

  • The calculation uses additive facet locations. In the default observed-exposure mode, interaction fits give an additive reference profile, not information under the full predictor; explicit plans refuse them. Two-family GPCM is unsupported in both modes.

  • G-Study/D-Study targets observed-score G/Phi. Neither that target nor an optimal allocation follows from this conditional information calculation.

References

  • Andrich, D. (1978). A rating formulation for ordered response categories. Psychometrika, 43, 561-573.

  • Masters, G. N. (1982). A Rasch model for partial credit scoring. Psychometrika, 47, 149-174.

  • Muraki, E. (1992). A generalized partial credit model: Application of an EM algorithm. Applied Psychological Measurement, 16, 159-176. doi:10.1177/014662169201600206 . Probability kernel and score derivative.

  • Muraki, E. (1993). Information functions of the generalized partial credit model. Applied Psychological Measurement, 17, 351-363. doi:10.1177/014662169301700403 . Equation 10 gives the information identity.

  • Samejima, F. (1974). Normal ogive model on the continuous response level in the multidimensional latent space. Psychometrika, 39, 111-121. General information formula specialized to GPCM by Muraki (1993).

Plot types

  • "tif": overall design-weighted precision across theta.

  • "se" / "sem" / "csem": conditional SEM across theta.

  • "both": precision and conditional SEM together, useful for presentations.

  • "iif": facet-level contribution curves for one selected facet in a supported RSM, PCM, or GPCM fit.

Returned data when draw = FALSE

draw = FALSE returns the reusable ggplot without printing it. plot_data(p) exposes the underlying plot, information_long, conditional_sem, summary and settings payloads. The overall curve comes from x$tif; facet contributions come from x$iif filtered to the selected facet. For an explicit plan, rating_plan, plan_settings and notes retain its counts, calibration basis and interpretation limits.

See also

fit_mfrm(), plot(x)

compute_information(), mfrmr_plot_migration

Examples

# Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below.
# example("compute_information", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
toy <- load_mfrmr_data("example_operational")
fit <- fit_mfrm(toy, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
                 method = "MML", model = "RSM",
                 quad_points = 7, maxit = 30)
info <- compute_information(fit)
head(info$tif)
info$tif$Theta[which.max(info$tif$Information)]
} # }
# One rating per selected rater and criterion, using a saved calibration.
fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "operational-mml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))$fit
plan <- unique(fit$prep$data[c("Rater", "Criterion")])
plan$Count <- 1L
planned <- compute_information(fit, rating_plan = plan)
head(planned$tif)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   Theta Information    SE
#>   <dbl>       <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 -6          0.166  2.45
#> 2 -5.94       0.176  2.38
#> 3 -5.88       0.187  2.31
#> 4 -5.82       0.198  2.25
#> 5 -5.76       0.210  2.18
#> 6 -5.7        0.223  2.12
plot(planned, type = "both", draw = FALSE)
# Optional workflow; run the example explicitly as shown below.
# example("plot.mfrm_information", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_operational")
fit <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
                 method = "MML", model = "RSM",
                 quad_points = 7, maxit = 30)
info <- compute_information(fit)
  tif_data <- plot(info, type = "tif", draw = FALSE)
  head(plot_data(tif_data, "plot"))
  iif_data <- plot(info, type = "iif", facet = "Rater", draw = FALSE)
  head(plot_data(iif_data, "plot"))
} # }
